page: Amazon Web Services c8id.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro system. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs spanning 24 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at up to 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 96 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU allocation typical of compute-focused platforms. In addition to high-throughput compute hardware, the instance includes 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 22 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong execution performance across vector, integer, and compression tasks. The processor provides hardware support for AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), delivering top-tier marks in Geekbench image processing and text processing tests, as well as strong Clang software compilation throughput. Synthetic benchmarks show robust read-only memory bandwidth measuring up to 3859.38 GB/sec in-cache and 194.95 GB/sec out-of-cache. Single-threaded and multi-threaded decompression tests achieve high throughput alongside strong Redis operations exceeding 86 million operations per second.

The 2:1 memory-to-core ratio limits suitability for monolithic in-memory databases that require high RAM density. However, the inclusion of 2850 GB of low-latency NVMe instance storage balances this profile by enabling high-IOPS local caching, scratch storage, and rapid intermediate state processing without additional network storage attachments. The instance provides strong compute efficiency for parallel build pipelines, batch data processing, CPU-based matrix operations, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The platform supplies 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and a 480 MB L3 cache, paired with 96 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory. Storage is handled locally by 2850 GB of bundled NVMe SSD space alongside 22 Gbps of baseline networking. Compute benchmarks show strong multi-core execution, with AMX and AVX-512 extensions driving top-decile scores in Geekbench text and image processing. High read memory bandwidth and strong compression rates support demanding I/O workloads. While the 2 GB per vCPU ratio makes it unsuited for large memory-resident datasets, the integrated fast NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for CI/CD compilation, distributed caching, CPU-driven inference, and batch analytics.
